title: Buck-Boost Converter (inverting)
summary: Non-isolated inverting converter; in continuous conduction the output magnitude equals the input scaled by D / (1 - D), with inverted polarity.

ports.name: in
ports.description: Positive input supply rail feeding the high-side switch.

ports.name: sw
ports.description: Switching node shared by the switch, the inductor, and the rectifier.

ports.name: out
ports.description: Inverted (negative) regulated output rail across the filter capacitor and load.

ports.name: pwm
ports.description: Gate-drive command for the switch from the controller.

parameters.name: Vout
parameters.description: Target regulated output voltage magnitude (output polarity is inverted).

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Steady-state duty cycle of the switch.

parameters.name: R_load
parameters.description: Load resistance seen at the output (R_load = |Vout| / Iout).

parameters.name: r_L
parameters.description: Inductor series resistance (DCR); dominant loss term and the cause of the gain roll-off at high duty cycle.

parameters.name: r_C
parameters.description: Output capacitor equivalent series resistance (ESR); sets the high-frequency zero.

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio
design_equations.description: Ideal CCM DC conversion ratio (inverting; magnitude can be below or above Vin).

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio_with_losses
design_equations.expression: |Vout| / Vin = D / ((1 - D) + r_L / ((1 - D) * R_load))
design_equations.description: CCM DC conversion ratio magnitude including the inductor series resistance r_L (Alonso eq. 3.8); r_L makes the gain peak and then roll off as D -> 1 instead of climbing without bound.

design_equations.name: inductor_current
design_equations.description: Average inductor current (Alonso eq. 3.10); the inductor carries both input and output current contributions.

design_equations.name: inductor_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak inductor current ripple in CCM (Alonso eq. 3.34).

design_equations.name: peak_device_current
design_equations.description: Peak current through the switch, diode, and inductor in CCM (Alonso summary, i_sp = i_dp).

design_equations.name: switch_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak blocking voltage across the switch (and the diode) is the sum of input and output magnitudes (Alonso eq. v_sp = v_dp = VB + Vo) - higher device stress than buck or boost.

design_equations.name: output_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in CCM (Alonso eq. 3.35); the capacitor alone supplies the load during the on-time. ESR adds r_C times the diode current step.

design_equations.name: boundary_load_resistance
design_equations.description: CCM-DCM boundary load resistance (Alonso eq. 3.37): CCM when R_load < R_lim, DCM when R_load > R_lim.

design_equations.name: boundary_output_current
design_equations.expression: Io_lim = Vout * (1 - D)**2 / (2 * L * fsw) = Vin * D * (1 - D) / (2 * L * fsw)
design_equations.description: Output current at the CCM-DCM boundary (Alonso eq. 3.36).

design_equations.name: dcm_conversion_ratio
design_equations.expression: |Vout| / Vin = D / sqrt(k),  k = 2 * L * fsw / R_load
design_equations.description: DCM DC conversion ratio magnitude (Alonso eq. 3.46-3.47); load-dependent and, unlike CCM, keeps rising with D.

design_equations.name: dcm_output_ripple
design_equations.expression: dVout = L * (D * Vin / (L * fsw) - Vout / R_load)**2 / (2 * Vout * C)
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in DCM (Alonso eq. 3.51).

design_equations.name: rhp_zero
design_equations.expression: f_rhpz = (1 - D)**2 * R_load / (2 * pi * D * L)
design_equations.description: Right-half-plane zero frequency of Gd(s) (zero at s = (1-D)**2 * R_load / (D*L)); it adds gain while subtracting phase, so it caps the achievable loop bandwidth and falls with both load and duty cycle.

design_equations.name: ccm_characteristic_polynomial
design_equations.description: Shared CCM denominator of every small-signal transfer function below (identical form to the boost); a complex pole pair whose resonance moves with the duty cycle.

design_equations.name: control_to_output_tf_ccm
design_equations.expression: Gd(s) = Vout(s)/d(s) = Vout*R_load*((1 - D)/D)*(1 - (D*L/((1 - D)**2*R_load))*s)*(1 + r_C*C*s) / Den(s)
design_equations.description: Control-to-output transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 3.21); note the right-half-plane zero factor (1 - (D*L/((1-D)**2*R_load))*s) and the ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C).

design_equations.name: audio_susceptibility_tf_ccm
design_equations.expression: Gb(s) = Vout(s)/Vin(s) = R_load*D*(1 - D)*(1 + r_C*C*s) / Den(s)
design_equations.description: Input-to-output (audio susceptibility) transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 3.24); same poles as Gd(s) but no right-half-plane zero.

design_equations.name: output_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop output impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 3.31); identical to the boost (k_sl = k_do = D in both), with Zo(0) = 0 and Zo(inf) approx r_C.

design_equations.name: input_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop input impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 3.27); the characteristic polynomial appears in the numerator divided by D**2, with Zi(0) = (1 - D)**2*R_load/D**2 and Zi(inf) -> infinity.

control_notes: The inverting buck-boost control-to-output transfer function Gd(s) contains a right-half-plane (RHP) zero at f_rhpz = (1-D)**2*R_load/(2*pi*D*L) whose frequency drops with both load and duty cycle - even more restrictive than the boost because of the extra D in the denominator. Voltage-mode loop bandwidth must stay well below f_rhpz, which forces a slow loop; current-mode control is preferred but the RHP zero remains. The switch and diode both block Vin + |Vout|, so device stress is higher than buck or boost. In discontinuous conduction (DCM, when R_load > R_lim = 2*L*fsw/(1-D)**2) the plant collapses to a first-order response and the RHP zero moves to very high frequency, so a light-load DCM design can run a faster loop. All small-signal results follow from the averaged dependent-source model: the switch is replaced by its average current source and the diode by its average voltage source, then linearized about the DC operating point. Account for the inverted output polarity in the feedback network and when reading V(out).

reference.source: J. Marcos Alonso, Modelling, Control and Simulation of DC-DC Converters
